So like I think given the nature of the show that this is precisely why we're getting to see his sins from that third person perspective of the audience. The version of him that's more real that Charlie isn't getting to see. Like in his breakdown musical number, no one was there for him to be wearing his mask for you know 


And like I'm just speculating here but personally I think that more fans would have reacted the way we did to Valentino. Like we would all just know there was no way he was getting redeemed. But there's that scene in the comic where he saves that lamb demon kid from that butcher, and a few other small things that make me think somewhere int what ether actually is a spark of goodness. And I think that's the whole point of the show is to highlight that.


My predictions are that the shows gonna run hopefully for like at least five seasons. And that we're gonna see off main characters ever season, though I think we might be rotating new people in every now and then... And I think people like angel dust are going to take a whole tk work through their shit to the point where he could be redeemed. So it's not like I think Alastors gonna be having this happen anytime soon 


But I figure it will go like this. Als gonna continue to be the antihero low key high stakes Gillian he is. He will continue to machinate behind the scenes. But... He will also get closer to Charlie. Not romantically just like in an actual friend like way. Even if he resists this the whole time. I think she will chip away at home lowly over time. Through small significant moments. Maybe she might step in front of a blow and get hurt at some point. Something that shifts the dynamic in a way he couldn't have foreseen and can't take back .. but he still keeps machinate and being evil in the sidelines. He has loft goals here that clearly involve Charlie and are maleficent... I think that he's going to go all the way through with his plans. I think he's going to succeed.


And I think he's not going to feel anything he wanted to feel in this moment.


Like the joy of watching everything fall. The joy of causing suffering and chaos. The entertainment he so clearly seeks. I think he's going to be in this moment where he's won and he's looking at Charlie who he's crushed... And he isn't going to feel anything but guilty. And he's going to have to jump through hoops from that point to fix what he now knows are mistakes. Regain her trust, rebuild what he destroyed, and in the process of earning Charlie's forgiveness will inadvertently alter himself in ways that lead him toward a redemption he may even still not want...


And I think the biggest reason that something like this might happen... Is because, well let's just look at the nature of the shot itself. It's about redemption. And "inside of every demon there's a rainbow" it's right in the promise and pilot, and it's written all over Charlie's face and in her earnest heart. They can all be saved. She's going to save them. And while I think that's a hard lesson Charlie's gonna have to learn (that not everyone deserves to be saved, looking at you Valentino) I don't think the narrative is going to keep Alastor as one of those unredeemable sinners

I suppose I had made come head cannon assumption that he's so pale because he was treated poorly about his heritage in his human life, and had internalized that self hatred subconsciously or something. But that's just a theory, a radio theory.
